title: The least squares RBF-PU method for linear elasticity in the diaphragm geometry
summary: The human diaphragm is vital for respiration and its simulation can aid in further understanding complications arising in individuals that have been subjected to mechanical ventilation. The diaphragm geometry is very thin and hence its numerical simulation poses a challenge for most numerical methods. In this paper, we compute the deformation of real diaphragm geometries which are modelled as linearly elastic and are subject to realistic boundary conditions.
